Cycling in Palm Springs

Flat valley miles, two climbs, the Tour in February

Getting around. The rules.

Palm Springs is a winter riding town at the west end of the Coachella Valley. The flat miles are on CV Link, the car-free path that runs 20 miles from the Palm Springs Visitor Center to Cathedral City. The two climbs are Tramway Road in town and Highway 74 out of Palm Desert. The Tour de Palm Springs, the valley’s big charity ride, starts downtown on South Palm Canyon on a Saturday in February; in 2027 that is February 6. The airport is two miles from downtown. Delta and American check a packed bike as a standard bag, $45 each way (Oct 2026). One Palm Desert shop builds a shipped bike, and three valley shops rent carbon road bikes. Bring yours for a week; rent for the Tour alone.

Best months
October to April. The Tour de Palm Springs FAQ puts February highs at 60 to 70 and lows at 50 to 55. PJAMM puts June-to-September highs at the foot of Highway 74 at 102 to 108 F and says not to start after sunrise then; Velo Palm Springs gives Joshua Tree a riding window of roughly October to April. The Desert Bicycle Club’s weekend rides are on its calendar from October, and Big Wheel Bikes’ Palm Springs store closes for the summer.
Nearest airport
Palm Springs International (PSP), 2 mi

Clubs and collectives in Palm Springs

  1. Desert Bicycle Club

    The Coachella Valley’s road club, based in Palm Desert. Guests are welcome and there’s no sign-up, but you need to be comfortable in a group, and no aerobars. A groups (drop) and B groups (regroup) go out most mornings: the Saturday rides (Saturdays, 7:30 am) from Palm Desert Civic Park, Sunday Climbers (Sundays, 7:30 am) up Highway 74, a winter Monday ride to Palm Springs (Mondays, 7:30 am), and weekday rides from Coffee Bean on El Paseo and from Bike N Brews that aren’t in the directory yet; the club’s calendar has them. From November the easier C rides (20 to 35 miles, about 13 to 14 mph) start from a different place each time and are posted on the club’s C Rides Facebook page.

    In the directory: Desert Bicycle Club Saturday Rides (Saturdays, 7:30 am) →

  2. Tri-A-Bike

    A Palm Desert bike shop at 44841 San Pablo Ave, (760) 340-2840. Its weekly fun ride (Saturdays, 10:30 am) leaves from the front of the store, and all types of bikes are welcome; the page says the rides start in October 2026. Distance and pace aren’t posted, so call before your first one. The same page lists the shop’s local routes and links a RideWithGPS account of Palm Springs-area rides.

    In the directory: Tri-A-Bike Saturday Fun Ride (Saturdays, 10:30 am) →

  3. Big Wheel Bikes CV

    Shops in Palm Springs and Palm Desert. Its community group rides, demo days, clinics and bike nights run in the November-to-April season and go up on its Instagram and Facebook, not on a fixed weekly slot, so follow the shop before you come. The Palm Springs store closes for the summer.

  4. Great Outdoors (Palm Springs chapter)

    LGBTQ+

    An all-volunteer LGBTQIA+ and allies outdoor club with five Southern California chapters, Palm Springs among them; cycling and mountain biking are on its list. The latest Palm Springs bike outing a page showed was a Gay History Bike Ride in March 2025, about 18 miles from the Mizell Senior Center. Events are for members unless noted, so join before you plan on one.

How Palm Springs rides: the zones, getting here

About Palm Springs

Palm Springs sits at the west end of the Coachella Valley, and the riding runs the length of it: Cathedral City, Rancho Mirage, Palm Desert, Indian Wells, La Quinta and Indio down Highway 111, with Desert Hot Springs across Interstate 10. This guide covers all of them. Its zones: Palm Springs itself (downtown, Tramway Road, the Visitor Center where CV Link starts); the valley floor along CV Link and Highway 111; the climbs, Tramway Road in town and Highway 74 south out of Palm Desert; and the car days, Box Canyon at the east end of the valley and Joshua Tree National Park over the hills to the north. Every listing says which one it sits in. The group rides are in Palm Desert, about 12 miles down the valley, so a rider sleeping downtown rides to them or drives.

The Tour de Palm Springs is on this site’s 2027 calendar: Saturday, February 6, 2027, routes from 16 to 101 miles from South Palm Canyon downtown, run by CVSPIN and Perimeter Bicycling for Coachella Valley charities. Robert is riding it. Packet pickup is Friday noon to 8 p.m. and Saturday from 6 a.m. at South Palm Canyon and Baristo; the century rolls at 6:30 and the 16-mile route at 9:30 (the Tour’s FAQ and registration page, Oct 2026). The organizer says the 2027 routes use CV Link where they can and the maps were still to come when we read the page. The valley’s group riding runs through one club, the Desert Bicycle Club in Palm Desert, whose calendar is public and whose rides take guests with no sign-up.

Riding in Palm Springs

The ride for the day you land is CV Link: the paved, car-free path from the Palm Springs Visitor Center at Highway 111 and Tramway Road, along the Whitewater River to Date Palm Drive in Cathedral City. 20 miles, join anywhere, turn around anywhere. Tramway Road starts at the same corner: 4 miles and 1,900 feet at 9.5 percent, steepening all the way, and bikes stop at the tramway’s toll gate about half a mile below the top. The big climb is Highway 74 south out of Palm Desert, 14 miles and 3,700 feet, with little or no shoulder past the first few miles and traffic at highway speed. The easy town loop is Velo Palm Springs’ 8-mile Midcentury Modern ride through downtown’s landmark houses. Palm Desert and Rancho Mirage, where CV Link has its gap, ride on a 14-mile loop from Tri-A-Bike’s door. The car days are Box Canyon from Mecca, Joshua Tree’s Park Boulevard, and Geology Tour Road for dirt. In the hot months, roughly May to October, start at dawn or don’t start: PJAMM puts June-to-September highs in Palm Desert at 102 to 108 F.

The group rides are in Palm Desert, and they take guests with no sign-up. The Desert Bicycle Club’s Saturday rides (Saturdays, 7:30 am) leave Palm Desert Civic Park in four groups, two that drop and two that regroup. Its Sunday Climbers (Sundays, 7:30 am) ride Highway 74 from the Starbucks at El Paseo at your own pace, regrouping at the Art Smith Trailhead and the Vista Point. In winter its Monday ride to Palm Springs (Mondays, 7:30 am) leaves Bike N Brews on Highway 111 and turns at Koffi in Rancho Mirage. Tri-A-Bike’s fun ride (Saturdays, 10:30 am) from the shop on San Pablo is the slow one, any bike. In Palm Springs itself, Big Wheel Bikes’ community rides run November to April and go up on the shop’s Instagram and Facebook, not on a fixed day, so follow the shop before you come. The club’s easier C rides, 20 to 35 miles at about 13 to 14 mph, start from a different place each week and are posted on its C Rides Facebook page. The rides hub for the valley is /rides/ca/palm-desert/.

The 9 routes, with maps →

Getting to Palm Springs

Fly into Palm Springs International (PSP), about two miles east of downtown; Tahquitz Canyon Way runs from the terminal to Palm Canyon Drive. Alaska, Southwest, United, Delta, American, WestJet, Air Canada and Sun Country fly it, much of it winter-only (a flight-search page, Oct 2026). Rental car counters are in the terminal’s north wing; SunLine buses carry a built bike on a front rack but not a case. Driving, downtown Los Angeles is about 100 miles west and downtown Phoenix about 260 miles east in a straight line; the road is longer. You don’t need a car for the Tour or the valley floor: the start, packet pickup, a repair shop and a rental fleet are all in Palm Springs, and the Palm Desert shops deliver a rental to a hotel. Highway 74, Joshua Tree and Box Canyon are car days. The Bring-your-bike page has the airline rules, the shop that builds a shipped bike and SunLine’s bike rules.

Questions about riding in Palm Springs

Should I bring my bike to Palm Springs?

Yes, for anything longer than the Tour itself. Delta and American check a packed bike as a standard bag, $45 each way (Oct 2026), and Tri-A-Bike in Palm Desert receives a shipped bike, builds it for $150 and delivers it to a Palm Springs hotel for $50. Renting is fair for a one-ride trip: Big Wheel Bikes on South Palm Canyon and two Palm Desert shops rent carbon road bikes at $100 to $140 a day and deliver (Oct 2026), with a two-day minimum on Tour weekend at two of them. No shop lists frame sizes, and no gravel rental was found.

Do I need a car to ride in Palm Springs?

Not for the Tour de Palm Springs or the valley floor. The airport is two miles from downtown, the Tour starts and packet pickup happens downtown, Trek’s repair shop and Big Wheel’s rentals are on South Palm Canyon, and CV Link runs 20 miles out of town without a car. The group rides start in Palm Desert, about 12 miles down the valley; ride there or drive. Highway 74, Joshua Tree and Box Canyon are car days.

Where does the Tour de Palm Springs start?

Downtown, on South Palm Canyon Drive between Baristo and Tahquitz. In 2027 the ride is Saturday, February 6: the century rolls at 6:30 a.m. and the 16-mile route at 9:30, and packet pickup is Friday noon to 8 p.m. and Saturday from 6 a.m. at South Palm Canyon and Baristo (the Tour’s FAQ and registration page, Oct 2026). Koffi Palm Springs Central on Tahquitz Canyon Way opens at 6:30, and Sherman’s Deli two blocks east opens at 8 for the plate afterward.

Where do group rides start near Palm Springs?

In Palm Desert, and guests are welcome with no sign-up. The Desert Bicycle Club’s Saturday rides (Saturdays, 7:30 am) leave Palm Desert Civic Park at 43900 San Pablo Ave in four groups; its Sunday Climbers (Sundays, 7:30 am) leave the Starbucks at Highway 74 and El Paseo for the climb; in winter its Monday ride to Palm Springs (Mondays, 7:30 am) leaves Bike N Brews at 73865 Highway 111. Tri-A-Bike’s fun ride (Saturdays, 10:30 am) leaves the shop at 44841 San Pablo Ave, any bike. In Palm Springs, Big Wheel Bikes’ community rides are posted on the shop’s social accounts, November to April. The valley’s rides hub is /rides/ca/palm-desert/.

Is CV Link finished, and can I ride it end to end?

It’s finished as planned, but it isn’t one path. CVAG opened about 40 miles in 2025 in three pieces: 20 miles from the Palm Springs Visitor Center to Date Palm Drive in Cathedral City, 5 miles in Palm Desert, and 16 miles from La Quinta to Coachella. Rancho Mirage and Indian Wells pulled out, so the gaps between the pieces are on the road. There are no posted hours, solar lights mark it at night, and you share it with e-bikes, scooters and golf carts held to 20 mph (CVAG, Oct 2026). Check CVAG’s map for closures before a long ride.

When is Palm Springs too hot to ride?

Roughly May to October. PJAMM puts June-to-September highs at the foot of Highway 74 at 102 to 108 F and says not to start after sunrise then; Velo Palm Springs puts Joshua Tree’s riding window at October to April and says the park’s summer temperatures have reached 124 F; the Coachella Valley Independent (April 2026) tells CV Link users to ride early or late in summer. The season is October to April. The Tour de Palm Springs FAQ puts February highs at 60 to 70 and lows at 50 to 55.
